summary.name: A Practical Guide to SLAs
summary.one_liner: A Catchpoint blog essay in which a former DoubleClick QoS lead explains how he built service level agreement (SLA) management after a costly 2001 penalty episode.
use_cases: Setting up an SLA management practice
Measuring third-party vendor performance in SLAs
Aligning internal targets with customer-facing SLAs
Building SLA breach reporting and alerts
summary.what_it_does: The article defines SLAs, SLOs and their key principles (attainable, repeatable, measurable, meaningful, mutually acceptable). It describes a Service Level Management approach built on four pillars (Administration, Monitoring, Reporting, Compliance) and an SLA lifecycle. It explains monitoring advice such as testing frequently from many vantage points, and a method called Differential Performance Measurement that compares a page with and without a third-party ad call to isolate vendor impact. It also covers reporting with Green/Yellow/Red status and real-time breach alerts.
notable: Introduces Differential Performance Measurement (DPM), comparing pages with and without a third-party call to remove noise
Firsthand account of a 2001 SLA penalty crisis, with over $1 million paid to one customer
Recommends aligning external SLAs with much tighter internal SLOs
caveats: Describes practices from the early 2000s at DoubleClick; tools mentioned, such as DigitalFuel and SiteScope, are dated or no longer exist
Not a product page; it is a single-author essay with no concrete templates or downloadable tooling
